svg.title: Who owns what, and for how long
svg.desc: Node-lifetime objects (component, SchedulerRos, Scheduler and its graph/collision/cost members) versus the per-call ScheduleContext created inside Plan().

g.text: Why const methods can still plan

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Scheduler's planning methods are const: they never change the Scheduler. Everything that

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: changes during planning lives in *ctx. A const method may still modify the object a

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Who owns what, and for how long

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Two lifetimes matter. The node keeps one Scheduler with its graphs and cost model; every plan request gets a fresh ScheduleContext that holds all mutable planning
